question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & x \end{bmatrix}$. Find all real $x$ for which $|A|=2$.
explanation:
Compute the determinant of the matrix.
$|A| = \begin{vmatrix} x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & x \end{vmatrix}$.
Expand along the first row.
$x\begin{vmatrix}x&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix} -1\begin{vmatrix}1&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}1&x\\1&1\end{vmatrix}$.
Compute each minor.
$\begin{vmatrix}x&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}=x^2-1$, $\begin{vmatrix}1&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}=x-1$, $\begin{vmatrix}1&x\\1&1\end{vmatrix}=1-x$.
Substitute into the expression.
$=x(x^2-1)-(x-1)+(1-x)$.
Simplify.
$=x^3-3x+2$.
Set the determinant equal to $2$.
$x^3-3x+2=2$.
$x^3-3x=0$.
Factorize.
$x(x^2-3)=0$.
Thus $x=0$, $x=\sqrt{3}$, or $x=-\sqrt{3}$.
